If I wouldn't have forced myself to lift and stuff my face with cottage cheese and eggs like I do I would probably be a bony shambling wreck since my meds have taken away all of my appetite over long periods of time.

In the medical field, you know your mental health patients (especially psychotic or schizophrenics) are taking their meds if become fat and miserable over time. Not all psych meds cause weight gain but meds like clozaril, seroquel, geodon, Zyprexa, Haldol ect definitely can cause weight gain as they tend to increase ACTH which stimulates the adrenal glands to release cortisol. These patients tend to carry their weight in their midsection, upper arms, chest (Breast development in males is definitely common) and in their neck and back love handles.

I worked with a child with chronic psychosis who, at age 14, is almost 170 lbs regardless of his diet (he is on a low glycemic, cardiac diet with max of 1200 cal/day) he gains around 5-10 lbs with each increase of his clozaril.

But of course there are lazy fat people who will gain weight on their meds because they refuse to adjust their diet to offset the side effects of increased appetite.

But try to judge carefully. Especially if that person was slim to average build before starting anti-psychotic/mood stabilizing medication. (Lithium and other mood stabilizers can cause hypothyroidism, the kid I worked with was on 2 mood stabilizers AND an anti-psychotic)
